items.question: What auspicious deception of time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The deception is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The verse opens a request for teaching about overcoming time.

items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: How is death destroyed according to the teaching being given?
premises: Death is destroyed in the manner described.
items.inference: The verse assures that the method destroys death.
uncertainties: The exact method is supplied in following verses.
items.plain_english: I tell you without doubt: thus death is destroyed.

items.question: Why does even a wise person burn at the tip of nectar?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar.
The instrument is the essence of juice.
items.inference: The verse warns that nectar practice can burn even the wise.
uncertainties: Whether dahyamāna describes the practitioner or the nectar.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person burns at the tip of nectar with the essence of juice.

items.question: How should air be drunk in this nectar practice?
premises: Air is placed at the root of tongue and palate.
The verb is optative, indicating prescription.
items.inference: The verse prescribes slowly drinking air after placing it at the tongue-palate root.
uncertainties: Whether pibec is third person or impersonal prescription.
items.plain_english: Having placed air at the root of tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

items.question: What happens to old age and death after one year of practice?
premises: Old age and death are the subject.

uncertainties: Whether abhyastañ modifies practice or air.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: Does poison enter the body even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
items.inference: The verse claims immunity to serpent poison in the body.
uncertainties: Whether daṃśito modifies the practitioner or another subject.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if bitten by great serpents.
